descriptionChirho: The proper noun חֹרֵב / חוֹרֵב designating Mount Horeb, the mountain of God in the wilderness, identified in Deuteronomic tradition with Sinai. The name means 'waste, desert' (from חרב 'to be dry'). Used with various prepositions: בְּחֹרֵב 'in/at Horeb' (Exod 17:6; Deut 1:6, 4:10, 4:15, 5:2, 9:8, 18:16, 29:1; 1 Kgs 8:9; 2 Chr 5:10; Ps 106:19; Mal 4:4), מֵחֹרֵב 'from Horeb' (Deut 1:2, 1:19), and the directional חֹרֵבָה 'Horeb-ward' (Exod 3:1), as well as absolute standalone uses (Exod 33:6; 1 Kgs 19:8). These are all inflectional variants of one proper noun, not different senses. Multilingual glosses uniformly render it as a place name: Arabic حُورِيبَ, German Horeb/Horev, Korean 호렙/호렛, Spanish Horeb/Jorev, Hindi होरेब, French Horeb.
